newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close up nearly one pct again.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close up nearly one pct again.

text.p: French shares, buoyed by market bullishness, headed higher on Monday to put on nearly another one percent after Friday's climb of 0.98 percent.

"It's bulls all the way," one broker said. Another said, "The market is well supported at these levels. It has good momentum." Paris is one of the markets which has not regained its all-time high and the CAC index has potential to hit 2,300 in the next few weeks, the second broker added.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.67 points or 0.96 percent at 2,277.14 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 18 at 2,277 from Friday's close.
Volume was a solid 5.2 billion francs.
Buying on the first December account day, positive trends in the dollar, bonds and Dow all contributed to the bullish trend.
The market will look for some profit-taking in the coming days but if there is more positive news, it could regain its all-time high of 2,360.98 hit in March 1994.
Operators do not want to go short in case there is a squeeze, but they want fresh impetus to push ahead.
Retialer Carrefour adds 2.08 percent to 3,093 franc, a consistent favourite among international investors.

Water firm Lyonnaise des Eaux puts on 3.49 percent to 489. It staged a catch-up as brokerages, including Cheuvreux de Virieu, Paribas Capital Markets and Dupont-Denant, confirmed buy recommendations after the utility's announcement of a buy-out offer for its Elyo heating unit.
Cie Generale des Eaux, up 0.78 percent at 646 francs, has consistently outperformed Lyonnaise in recent months, as chairman Jean-Marie Messier charmed the market.

Carmakers PSA firmed 1.96 percent to 624, Renault gained three percent to 120, while tyre company Michelin added 2.17 percent to 263.5. Brokers said the lira's ERM re-entry would relieve the competitive threat from Fiat for French firms.
